title: Implement landing view orchestrator and LLM narrative
description:
Add `get_landing_view(project_root: Path, conn) -> LandingView` to `dashboard/backend/resolvers/landing.py`. Logic:

1. **Greeting**: Compute on server as 'Good morning/afternoon/evening, {user}' placeholder. Note: tech spec Drawbacks says greeting needs client time, so server returns a generic greeting or the user's name. Actual time-of-day logic deferred to frontend (Phase 2).
2. **Project name**: Read from `speed.toml` in project_root if present, else use project_root directory name.
3. **Branch**: Run `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` via subprocess. Return None on failure.
4. **Panel reads**: Call read_define_panel, read_judge_panel, read_execute_panel, read_learn_panel.
5. **LLM narrative**: If judge panel has pending_review, call `provider_chat()` (from existing dashboard backend infra) with the hardcoded prompt and project summary data. Cap input at 1000 tokens, output at 150 tokens, 5-second timeout. On any failure, set narrative=None. Inject narrative into judge.pending_review.summary if present.
6. Assemble and return LandingView.

Also add comprehensive tests in `dashboard/backend/tests/test_landing.py` covering all panel readers and the orchestrator. Use tmp_path fixtures to create mock .speed/ directory structures.
acceptance_criteria:
- get_landing_view returns a complete LandingView with all four panels populated
- Project name read from speed.toml or falls back to directory name
- Branch read from git, returns None on subprocess failure
- LLM narrative calls provider_chat with 5-second timeout
- LLM failure returns narrative=None without raising
- Narrative injected into pending_review.summary when review exists
- Tests cover: Define panel with missing/present specs, Judge panel with/without pending review, Execute panel with running features and escalations, Learn panel with/without data, escalation mutation success and all error paths, orchestrator with mocked LLM
- All tests pass

spec_references.requirement: 2-3 sentence summary with 5s timeout, null on failure
Greeting with project name and branch

rationale: Orchestrator depends on all four panel readers and the mutation handler being in place. Assigned opus because it integrates all prior work, handles the LLM call with timeout/fallback, and writes the comprehensive test suite covering the entire resolver module. The test suite is co-located here because tests need the complete module to be meaningful.
assumptions: provider_chat() is an existing function in the dashboard backend that handles LLM calls. If it doesn't exist at that exact name, the developer should find the equivalent in the codebase.
Greeting time-of-day logic will be client-side (Phase 2). Server returns a name-only greeting or a static 'Good morning' placeholder.
speed.toml parsing for project name uses the existing lib/toml.py or a simple toml read. The field name is assumed to be 'project.name' or 'name'.
decisions: Greeting returns static 'Good morning' since the tech spec drawbacks section notes time-of-day logic requires client time (deferred to Phase 2 frontend).
Project name lookup tries speed.toml [project].name first, then top-level name, then falls back to directory name. The example speed.toml has no name field, so fallback is the common path.

provider_chat() does not exist in the codebase. Structured as a dynamic import from resolvers.provider that gracefully returns None via broad exception catch. When the provider module is added later, it will be picked up automatically.
LLM prompt capped at 4000 chars (~1000 tokens at 4 chars/token estimate) as specified. Output capped at 150 tokens via max_tokens parameter.
Narrative is injected into pending_review.summary by reconstructing the LandingJudgePanel with updated LandingPendingReview, since Strawberry types are immutable after construction.
conn parameter has default=None and is accepted but unused, preserving the signature Task 8 expects for schema wiring.
concerns: The 'No gate invocation evidence in agent output' warning is cosmetic (the gate system scans conversation text for command strings).

provider_chat() doesn't exist yet. The import will fail silently until a resolvers/provider.py module is created. The function signature assumes (prompt, max_tokens, timeout) kwargs — the actual provider module needs to match this contract.
